clue.text: She modelled with Tessa and Maud, working under the latter's aegis

indicators.note: working here means set in motion and reshaped, so the names are rearranged

parts.note: the latter of Tessa and Maud is Maud, so her name is used a second time

explanation.surface: Two women do some modelling under the supervision of one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges TESSA, MAUD and MAUD again (the latter's) into the waxworks founder's name; 'under ... aegis' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of the famous London waxworks museum sculpted wax figures, so she modelled.

clue.text: To celebrate moving on, take him a gift

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: To mark someone leaving, you hand him a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges ON plus TAKE HIM A GIFT; the surface suggests a farewell party for someone moving on.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending a whole evening in festivities is an idiom for celebrating.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman upset an Italian lady

parts.note: Don is the Spanish courtesy title for a gentleman

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word an is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman has offended an Italian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AN into NA beneath DON.
explanation.definitionFit: Donna is the Italian title and word for a woman of rank.

clue.text: Gobbledygook from taciturn old boy coming over on plane

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent, so mum means taciturn

indicators.note: coming over means turning over, so the abbreviation for old boy is flipped

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a jumbo is a jumbo jet, a large aircraft

explanation.surface: Nonsense talk comes from a quiet former pupil flying in on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' turns OB into BO.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless jargon or nonsense is a synonym for gobbledygook.

clue.text: Young Jeremy Fisher produces a story about refugee with nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a story is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: a tale is a story
DP stands for displaced person, a refugee
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A youngster named Jeremy Fisher writes a tale about a destitute refugee.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Fisher is the frog in Beatrix Potter's children's tale, so his young form is a tadpole.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog begins life as a tadpole, so a juvenile frog is one.

clue.text: Keep up as units assemble

indicators.note: assemble means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something continues while military units gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assemble' rearranges AS plus UNITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain or prolong something is to sustain it.

clue.text: A new number to be put up shortly

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means raised, so the letters are read upward, in reverse

explanation.surface: A fresh telephone number is going to be displayed soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put up' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon or presently.

clue.text: Lorna's accepted the inducement to contribute

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R D Blackmore's novel, so Lorna's is Doone's
a fish that takes a lure bites, so bit means accepted the bait

explanation.surface: Lorna took the bribe in order to make a donation.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing your part in a joint effort is an idiom for contributing.

clue.text: Duke on American navy ship is without English money

parts.note: Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest

indicators.note: without means outside, so those letters go around the abbreviation for English

parts.note: USNS stands for United States Naval Ship
is shortens to 's, giving S

explanation.surface: A duke sailing on a US naval vessel has no English cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' puts USNS and S around E, giving USNESS after PROSPERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth or affluence, being well off, is what having plenty of money amounts to.

clue.text: Book about married woman who was given a golden handshake

definitions.text: who was given a golden handshake

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the book's name is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: Kings is a book of the Old Testament
Ida is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A book concerns a wife who received a generous retirement pay-off.
explanation.walkthrough: A golden handshake is a large payment on leaving a job; here it is taken literally of the legendary king whose touch turned things to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the king of Phrygia was granted the gift of turning whatever he touched into gold.

clue.text: Regard the round stern

parts.note: O is round in shape
dour means stern or severe

explanation.surface: Look at the circular back of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regard' is the noun meaning esteem: to be in good odour is to be well thought of.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean reputation or esteem, as in being in good or bad odour with someone.

clue.text: 'oly light enveloping American mission

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping around, so the dropped-H halo goes round the abbreviation for American

parts.note: a holy light is a halo; dropping the H, as the apostrophe in 'oly does, gives 'alo

explanation.surface: A Cockney-style holy glow surrounds an American missionary outpost.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'oly tells you to drop the H of halo too, as in Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in Texas was originally a Spanish mission before its famous siege.

clue.text: Approve of love with a girl

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
Kay is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone gives their blessing to a romance with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something the go-ahead or sanction it is to okay it.

clue.text: Flower found on the course

definitions.meaning: a flower is something that flows, a river; a river in north-east England
on a golf course, balls are placed on small pegs before driving off

explanation.definitionFit: A northern English river, and the pegs golfers use at the start of each hole.

clue.text: Tailor — he's undernourished

definitions.meaning: Robin ... is the tailor among the craftsmen in A Midsummer Night's Dream
a person or creature that is thin from lack of food

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tailor in A Midsummer Night's Dream, and a word for a starving, emaciated person.

clue.text: Take into account the letters in first down clue

annotationWithheld.why: Take into account the letters in first down clue: IN + CLU(D)E needs 'in' both as the letters IN and as the indicator putting D inside CLUE; no other word signals the insertion
annotationWithheld.clue: Take into account the letters in first down clue

clue.text: Called round on one occasion in vain

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for called goes around the other piece

parts.note: cited means called, as to a court
once means on one occasion

explanation.surface: Someone visited once without result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in vain' reads as 'uselessly', but 'vain' alone is the definition and 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being self-satisfied and proud of one's looks or abilities is a synonym for vain.

clue.text: It's remarkable how the Spanish stick around

indicators.note: around means turned round, so both pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a baton is a stick, as used by a conductor or relay runner

explanation.surface: It's striking how Spanish people keep loitering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns ELBATON backwards; 'stick around' looks like the phrase meaning stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of note, striking or distinguished is remarkable.

clue.text: Designations used on pencils with silver case

parts.note: pencils are graded H for hard and B for black, so H and B are the designations
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Labels on pencils come with a silver box.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' joining H and B is part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbag is a small carrying case for personal items.

clue.text: Peevish Marx has you in first place, not second

indicators.note: the Y is put in place of the second of the comedian's two O's, while the first one stays

parts.note: Groucho Marx was the comedian of the Marx Brothers
Y is a short form of you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A grumpy Marx puts you first rather than second.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy, bad-tempered and irritable describe someone peevish.

clue.text: Shakespearian character's hard speech cut

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the speech loses its final letter

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character's harsh speech has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last N of ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's loyal friend, who survives to tell the story, is a character in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Spaniard made a cache in the past, concealing some money

parts.note: hid means stored away secretly, made a cache

indicators.note: concealing means holding inside, so the word for in the past wraps round the money

parts.note: ago means in the past
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a sum of money

explanation.surface: A Spaniard once stashed something away, including some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts L inside AGO, giving ALGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish nobleman of the lower gentry.

clue.text: About finished

definitions.meaning: about meaning concerning, as in a fuss about something
finished meaning ended, as when a game is done

explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'concerning' as a preposition and 'ended' as an adjective.

clue.text: Student caught with a dictionary

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A student was caught carrying a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A coed is a female student at a mixed college, a mainly American usage.

clue.text: Those funny national characteristics

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: Those quaint national traits that foreigners find amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges THOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos means the distinctive spirit or character of a people or culture.

clue.text: Swell chap given a welcome

parts.note: a chap is a man, he
ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A fine fellow is greeted warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' reads as the slang adjective meaning great, but it is the verb for rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to rise and fall, as the sea swells.

clue.text: Raised the money, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for money is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: The cash was collected, so it's reported.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means brought up or reared, as children or animals are raised.

clue.text: Bury, where the season starts late

indicators.note: late means dead or gone, so the season's starting letter is missing

parts.note: winter is a season of the year

explanation.surface: In Bury, the season begins behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb; 'starts late' means the first letter, W, is dead and gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave.

clue.text: Belief that's about tax in till

parts.note: a cult is a system of religious belief

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation for that is goes round the tax

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, Latin for that is
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A faith that concerns tax being stored in the cash register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts VAT inside IE; 'till' looks like a cash register but is the verb for working soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To till land is to plough and prepare it for crops.

clue.text: Jervis Pendleton, alias the Crane-fly

definitions.meaning: the secret benefactor in Jean Webster's novel, whom the orphan heroine nicknames after his long shadow

explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Jean Webster's 1912 novel, and the common name of the long-legged insect.
